class.name: Paladin
class.text: Plate, mana and a seal. Seal of Righteousness, Holy Light and Devotion Aura are yours from the start, Judgement comes at 4, Holy Strike at 6. At 10 you get Seal of Fury, Righteous Fury and your first talent point. Every line below says what to have on you before it says what to press.

card.caresAbout: the seal on you, the aura and blessing you chose, Judgement and the mana to do it again
card.vocabulary: seal, judge, aura, blessing, swing, strike, cooldown, mana
card.soundsLike: calm and exact, one thing at a time. A paladin line says what is on you before it says what to press
card.neverSays: rage, stance, anything about the Light, faith, justice as an idea or a crusade (spells have those words and the line uses them as names only)
card.test: could the line be followed by someone who has never heard of the Light?

advice.say: Retribution is the build this page advises, because a seal does most of the work and it kills alone. The price: no taunt worth the name and no healing in a fight, so a dungeon wants a tank and a healer beside you.

Holy is the healer. The common road is to level in Retribution and move into Holy for dungeons, and this page puts the healing points first instead. The price: Holy kills slowly alone, so levelling takes longer.

Protection is the tank. The common road is to level in Retribution up to 40, and this page spends its first 12 points there. The price: Holy Shield only comes at 42, and the spec is slow to quest alone.

overview.who: You fight in melee with a seal on you and heal yourself between pulls. It is slow work and hard to kill, and it runs on mana, not rage.
overview.good: Staying alive while you hit things. A group wants your auras and blessings, and you can always heal yourself when the fight is over.
overview.bad: Speed and crowds. You kill one monster at a time and wait for mana between pulls, and until Consecration there is nothing for a pack.
overview.resource: Mana. Seals, Judgement, Holy Strike and heals spend it, and a swing costs none. When the bar is empty, keep swinging and sit down afterwards.
overview.levelling: Seal on, Judgement when it is ready, Holy Strike when it is ready, swing the rest of the time. Heal when the fight is over and drink when the bar is low. Aura and blessing go on before the first pull.
overview.ten: You get your first talent point and pick a spec. Retribution levels alone, Protection holds monsters for a group and Holy heals one. The first points usually go to Retribution, and the Holy page here does not. A respec costs gold.

damage.reason: A seal and Judgement do most of the work, so Retribution kills alone.

heal.reason: The only healing build. It kills slowly alone and is made for a group, so level in Retribution first if you like.

tank.reason: The only tanking build. Seal of Fury makes Judgement a taunt, and Consecration holds a pack.

builds.name: Retribution
builds.intro: Retribution fights in melee with one big weapon and a seal that adds to every swing. It is the Paladin that kills alone, and the price is no taunt worth the name and no healing in a fight. Judgement no longer uses the seal up, and Holy Strike is a second button, so the page is about which seal and when to change it.
builds.line: One big weapon, a seal, Judgement and Holy Strike. It kills alone, and a seal does most of the work.
builds.pathNote: (38 points in Retribution, 5 in Protection for Divine Intellect and 8 in Holy for Divine Strength and Improved Seals.)
builds.split: the first points. Deflection first, or Benediction first for mana. The last 13 points are ours: the common orders stop at 30, and the end is ours, from Divine Strength, Improved Seals, Holy Conduit and Divine Intellect.
builds.dry: Most of this page waits on Judgement. If it is not ready, hit the monster.

path.why: More parry, so fewer hits land, and a parry brings your next swing sooner. It is your safety while you learn what a pull costs.
Your spells and attacks crit more often. That includes the Holy damage on every swing.
Judgement comes back sooner. Most of your damage waits on it, so a shorter wait is more damage.
A swing sometimes adds Holy damage, and its Judgement hits a stunned monster harder. Take it with a slow weapon. With a fast one, keep Seal of Righteousness.
You run and ride faster. Between pulls it saves more time than any other talent here, which is the whole of its use.
Judgement sometimes gives back part of the seal's mana, so you drink less. More points make it likelier.
Holy Strike hits harder and refreshes the Judgement on its target. It keeps your Judgement up through a long fight.
Judgement sometimes gives back part of the seal's mana, so you drink less. More points make it likelier.
Physical and Holy damage go up while you hold a two-hander, and the threat you make goes down. Alone, threat is not your problem.
A humanoid stops until something hurts it. Use it on the second monster of a pull, or on a runner while you heal. It also leads to the capstone.
A critical strike raises your Physical and Holy damage for a few seconds, and it stacks. It needs the Seal of Command talent.
Some of your hits lower the monster's attack power for a while, so its blows hurt less and you heal less.
Part of your Intellect becomes spell damage, so your Holy spells hit harder with Intellect on your gear. It opens the row of the capstone.
Your swings store a copy of your seal, and changing seal spends the copies. It is why a long fight swaps seals.
Instant spells and abilities cost less. Seals, Judgement and Holy Strike are all instant, so you drink less.
Part of your Intellect becomes spell damage, so your Holy spells hit harder with Intellect on your gear.
More Intellect, which is more mana. With Champion of the Light it is also more Holy damage.
More Strength, which is more attack power on every swing. It leads to Improved Seals.
Your seals and Judgements deal more damage. It is the Holy tree's damage talent for a melee Paladin.

builds.name: Holy
builds.intro: Holy keeps people alive. It kills slowly alone, and a dungeon wants it. Holy Shock is both halves of the build, a heal on a friend and damage on an enemy, and Oath of Light and Light's Vigil are for the tank and the party.
builds.line: Heals the group. It levels slowly alone, and a dungeon wants it.
builds.pathNote: (33 points in Holy, 13 in Retribution for Benediction, Conviction, Sanctified Judgement and Pursuit of Justice, 5 in Protection for Divine Intellect.)
builds.split: when to leave Holy. This order puts the 31 healing points first. The other order levels in Retribution (Benediction, Holy Conduit, Improved Judgement, Pursuit of Justice) and moves into Holy later. Healing while levelling is slow, which is the price of this order.
builds.dry: A heal on a full bar is mana you do not have for the next one.

path.why: Your Flash of Light, Holy Light and Light's Vigil sometimes keep casting when you are hit. A healer casts under hits all day.
Part of your mana regeneration continues while you cast, and a healer casts all the time. It also opens Illumination.
Holy Light, Flash of Light and Holy Shock heal more. It is the plain healing talent, and every heal you cast is bigger for it.
A critical heal sometimes gives back mana. The more you heal, the less you drink. It needs 2 points in Reverence.
Swear it on the tank: your Holy Light, Flash of Light and Holy Shock heal that target more. It is the one-target healer's talent.
Your next Flash of Light, Holy Light or Holy Shock is sure to crit. With Illumination, a big heal on it can pay its own mana back.
A critical Holy Shock or Flash of Light makes your next Holy Light cast faster.
Your Holy spells hit more often, and silences on you end sooner. Holy Shock and Exorcism should not miss.
An instant heal on a friend, or Holy damage on an enemy. It is your quick heal and your way to kill alone, and it opens the last two talents.
Holy Shock crits more often on a friend who does not carry your Oath of Light. Heal the tank with Holy Light and everyone else with Holy Shock.
Your Holy spells hit more often, and silences on you end sooner. Holy Shock and Exorcism should not miss.
Consecration, Exorcism, Holy Wrath and Hammer of Wrath cost less. They are the spells you kill with between heals.
Your critical heals heal even more. With Divine Favor and Illumination it is the most the tree gives a healer who crits.
Mark one friend, and your next Holy Shock on them has no cooldown and heals them and their party. It costs a lot, so use it when four or more are hurt.
Instant spells and abilities cost less. Holy Shock, Judgement and Holy Strike are instant, so you drink less.
Your heals and attacks crit more often, which feeds Illumination.
More Intellect, which is more mana, and a healer is limited by mana.
Judgement sometimes gives back part of the seal's mana, so you drink less. More points make it likelier.
You run and ride faster. Between pulls it saves more time than any other talent here, which is the whole of its use.
Consecration, Exorcism, Holy Wrath and Hammer of Wrath cost less. They are the spells you kill with between heals.
Judgement sometimes gives back part of the seal's mana, so you drink less. More points make it likelier.
Cleanse and Purify cost less mana, and Exorcism and Holy Wrath come back sooner.

builds.name: Protection
builds.intro: Protection holds monsters on you and stays up. Seal of Fury makes Judgement a taunt, Holy Shield makes a block threat, and Consecration holds a pack. It is a shield and a magic tank, and mana is its limit.
builds.line: Holds the monsters on you with a shield. Slow to quest alone, strong in a group.
builds.pathNote: (35 points in Protection, 16 in Retribution: 12 first for Pursuit of Justice, 4 last.)
builds.split: when to go back to Protection. The other order takes Retribution first, then Protection with little room to choose, and has no Toughness, Sacred Duty, Shield Specialization or Iron Creed. This order has all four. Anticipation can move to Toughness or Guardian's Favor.
builds.dry: A monster still on you after 20 seconds means the job is working.

path.why: More parry, so fewer hits land, and a parry brings your next swing sooner. A hit that misses makes no work for the healer.
Judgement comes back sooner. It is a taunt with Seal of Fury, so a shorter wait is more control.
Your spells and attacks crit more often. It costs 3 points on the way to Pursuit of Justice.
You run and ride faster. This build spends the points on it in Retribution first and then goes back to Protection.
A hit on you sometimes raises your chance to block for a while. It is what makes the shield worth carrying, and Shield Specialization needs all 5.
You miss less. A tank's threat is Holy damage, and a missed attack makes none.
Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Templar's Bulwark come back sooner, and Forbearance ends sooner.
A shield worth your full health for a few seconds, for the one big hit. It shares Forbearance with Divine Protection, so use one or the other.
Your shield absorbs more, and a block can give back some mana. Mana is what limits a tank.
More armour from your gear, so every hit is smaller.
A second Judgement of your seal with a cooldown of its own. With Seal of Fury it is a second taunt, and it does not use up the seal.
While Righteous Fury is on, you take less damage from everything. Keep it on in a group.
More block for a short time and Holy damage on every block, which is threat. It is the button to press whenever its charges run out.
A block can give you a free attack, and it stores several. More swings are more threat.
More Defense, so you are hit and critically hit less. These points can move to Toughness or Guardian's Favor.
Holy Strike makes more threat, and with Righteous Fury on it also cuts the damage you take for a few seconds.
Holy Strike comes back sooner and strikes with your shield, so Holy Shield and Shield Specialization fire from it. You can also block spells for a time.
Judgement sometimes gives back part of the seal's mana, so you drink less. More points make it likelier.
Holy Strike hits harder and refreshes the Judgement on its target. It is the last Retribution point of the build.
